translation:
[Vadu Dhol ||18||, continued]

|| Valan ||

3. He sent home the one who had been unaware, having first made his life-breath pure.
4. The Supreme Self is the true abode; there the soul finds its rest.
5. In this way a single love-colour took hold, and the inner division was broken.

[Valan]
6. The inner division was broken in just this way: you yourself became Parbrahm (the Supreme Reality).
7. I was overtaken as the grub is overtaken by the wasp — such is the way of meditation upon You (one becomes what one contemplates).

[Aad 12]
1. Through remembrance and meditation one is absorbed in the nectar of pure consciousness; Hari, Hari — He comes as a cow comes to her calf.
2. Bound by His Name, Hari comes of His own accord; Hari, Hari — the Lord does not abandon His devotee in this perishing world.

[Valan]
3. Perishable is the companionship of worldly life; yet there the devotee has found the Lord.
4. You are Ram, the lover of devotees; true in its very meaning is Your Name.
5. The mind is set in aversion against prakriti (material nature); thus ever new are the guises You take.

[Valan]
6. Ever new are Your guises; serve the Lord Morar (Krishna) through His Name.
7. He who, knowing one to be a devotee, does not slight him — he alone, in this world.

[Aad 13]
1. Set about with ruby, pearl and gold — Hari, Hari — by sandal paste and flowers He is not pleased.
2. He who takes no delight in song, in music, in what is heard from scripture; Hari, Hari — though one dances before Him, He is not won over.
3. He who is pleased neither by cleverness nor by simplicity; Hari, Hari — how then shall we bring Him under our sway?

[Valan]
4. How shall we bring Him under our sway — He who is the father of Brahma and Shankar?
5. His own regard is this: where I myself am, there is My Name.
6. Wherever, wherever a devotee takes My Name, there, there is My abode.
7. There, there is My abode; there no one can work obstruction or terror.
8. Whoever serves Hari's Name to the very end — to him I grant a peerless dwelling.

[Aad 14]
[Tika (the commentary), Rag Godi]
1. Know Him to be such, and follow Him night and day; Hari, Hari — forsake this world, which is perishing.
2. The one imperishable is Narayan alone; Hari, Hari — He who created birth and death.
3. Those who have not been freed by this human birth; Hari, Hari — how will they be freed in any other birth?
4. Clinging to the objects of sense and driven along by household affairs; Hari, Hari — in vain is this excellent birth spent away.
5. Give up the objects of sense and turn your love to your own true good; Hari, Hari — O devotee, follow this Parbrahm.
6. Forms are only the vessels of the four wombs of creation; Hari, Hari — the primal formless One alone truly is.
7. Gods, sages, men, the unmoving and the moving; Hari, Hari — though You fashion and break them, no karma clings to You.
8. He who set sin and merit within the world; Hari, Hari — action and duty do not touch You.
9. He who created fire (Vaishvanar) with its heat; Hari, Hari — who can endure that burning of His?
10. He who brought forth the snows and the Himalaya; Hari, Hari — to what can His cooling quality be compared?
11. He who set the primal wind loose in the world; Hari, Hari — exceedingly great is that power of His.
12. He who gave knowledge to the god Maheshwar; Hari, Hari — knowledge itself does Him service.
13. All dharma and observance rest upon truth; Hari, Hari — higher still, I say, is the Name of Parbrahm.
14. The Vedas and Puranas declare it again and again; Hari, Hari — no other fruit weighs equal to the Name.
15. No end can be found to the glory and fruit of the Name; Hari, Hari — he who holds faith in it obtains that fruit.
16. Bind yourself with certainty to this one word; Hari, Hari — what austerity or rite need you then accomplish?
17. Tulsi, the Name, the tilak of gopichandan; Hari, Hari — no other fruit equals satsang (the company of saints).
18. Hold the word of scripture as certain; Hari, Hari — leave the lesser and take the greater.
19. Where the Name is absent and no thought of it ever comes; Hari, Hari — how then shall the supreme state be reached?
20. Setting aside His own mantra and inner teaching; Hari, Hari — He gave the Name to His own devotee.
21. All the rest He left entangled in disputes; Hari, Hari — those, that is, who have no faith in the Name.
22. He who has heaped up very much karma; Hari, Hari — in him faith does not arise.
23. Until karma is exhausted, faith does not arise; Hari, Hari — and lacking faith, one is born again.
24. Through crores of births, through vows, mantras and inner disciplines; Hari, Hari — it is in the last birth that faith comes.
25. Fasten the mind upon meditation on Parbrahm; Hari, Hari — even prescribed action lies in Parbrahm's hand.
26. Neither I nor anything of mine is my own; You and what is Yours alone truly are; Hari, Hari — all deeds and doings, O Lord, are in Your hand.
27. Thus lay claim to nothing and count nothing as your own; Hari, Hari — keep to good conduct and behold Narayan.
28. True and certain are You alone, O Lord; Hari, Hari — all else is perishing, false, and falling apart.
29. Whoever reads this dhol (song of praise) and reflects upon it; Hari, Hari — he is transformed and becomes Parbrahm.
30. This devotee, who is as nothing, makes his prayer, O Lord; Hari, Hari — may we obtain the refuge of the holy Guru.

Here the holy Vadu Dhol is complete ||18||
